name: Nahor
overview: Nahor, a male figure in Scripture, is uniquely identified as the son of Terah. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him. His role is primarily established through his lineage and familial connections.
namesAndTitles: Nahor is a proper name meaning 'the mound of Nahuru.' This name is not indicated as being given by God but is recorded in Genesis 11:27. The meaning reflects a personal or geographical identifier rather than a divine title.
familyAndRelationships: Nahor was the son of Terah and the husband of Milcah. He fathered several children, including Uz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel, as well as others through a concubine named Reumah, such as Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah. These relationships position him as a patriarch within his family line.
scriptureSignificance: Nahor's significance lies in his role as Abraham's brother and the progenitor of a family that remained in Mesopotamia while Abraham moved to Canaan. His descendants, notably Bethuel, became key figures as ancestors of Rebekah and Laban, linking Nahor's line to the patriarchal narrative through Isaac and Jacob. This lineage maintained important family ties and provided wives for Abraham's descendants, preserving a distinct family identity separate from the Canaanite peoples.
